title: Orchestrated capacity-slice handoff for non-disruptive kernel patching
creator: Rohan Patel
description: Background: Kernel / low-level runtime patches require host reboots across Dedicated fleets. Existing rolling drains cause noticeable throughput dips for heavy inference tenants because KV-cache warmup is slow and traffic is bursty. Goal: implement an orchestrated capacity-slice handoff that preserves per-tenant throughput contracts during planned kernel patch windows.
problem_statement: Planned host reboots for kernel or hypervisor patches lead to temporary throughput shortfalls for customers with high throughput guarantees. Current drain strategy (host-by-host) can create correlated KV-cache cold starts and a temporary 10-30% P95 latency spike for affected tenants.
proposal_summary: Introduce 'capacity-slices' (time-boxed throughput reservations) and a lease-backed handoff protocol where draining hosts donate warm KV-cache segments to reserved lanes, and traffic is smoothly shifted into pre-warmed lanes. Key components: slice allocator, lease ledger, warmup waves, progressive traffic shapers, and automated rollback on health regressions.
design_details: 1) Slice allocator: compute per-region/cluster slices based on current committed throughput and transient headroom. 2) Lease ledger: ephemeral, strongly-consistent record (etcd) of slice ownership and planned handoffs. 3) Warmup waves: before draining, allocate a warmup wave of hosts that prefetch KV pages for specific model sessions and prefix caches. 4) Traffic shaper: percentage-based traffic shift (0 -> 100 over N steps) pinned per-tenant route. 5) Health checks: combined readiness + latency guardrails (P95 < 1.5x baseline and error rate < 0.5%) before next step. 6) Fallback: automatic soft-fail to best-effort mode where we remove guarantees in emergency and notify SRE/PM.
acceptance_criteria:
- No committed tenant should see >10% reduction in reserved throughput during a scheduled maintenance window.
- P95 latency for guarded routes must not exceed 1.5x baseline for more than 5 minutes.
- Automated end-to-end canary (stage) completes with no rollback on two consecutive maintenance simulations.
- Rollout runbook validated and linked; on-call can restore normal drain within 10 minutes.
metrics_and_slo:
- Baseline targets: throughput preservation >= 95% of committed lanes, latency P95 <= 1.5x baseline, error rate delta <= 0.5 percentage points.
- Dashboards: per-slice throughput, KV cache hit-rate, slice-lease conflicts, traffic-shift progress.
- Alerts: slice-allocation-failure, health-check-violation, unexpected-rollbacks.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (Infra + Ledger): implement lease ledger and slice allocator (2 weeks). Phase 2 (Warmup + Shaper): add warmup wave coordination and traffic shaper (3 weeks). Phase 3 (Canary + Docs): run staged canaries in preprod clusters, author runbooks, integrate console observability (2 weeks). Phase 4 (Gradual Rollout): opt-in beta with 10% of customers on Dedicated for first month, then wider rollout.
- PRs: infra/lease-ledger, runtime/warmup-controller, routing/traffic-shaper.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Reservation overhead: reserving warm lanes increases idle GPU time and cost. We'll mitigate by dynamic rightsizing and reclaiming unused reservations.
- Complexity: the lease-backed model introduces a new state machine and failure modes (stale leases, split-brain). We'll add quorum checks and conservative timeouts.
- Observability gaps: require new per-slice metrics to troubleshoot; temporary blind spots could slow incident response.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for slice allocator and lease lifecycle.
- Integration tests: simulated drain with synthetic workload to measure KV warmup delta.
- Load test: 4h high-throughput run with progressive drains at 5%/step to validate throughput preservation.
- Chaos tests: kill pre-warmed hosts mid-shift to validate rollback safety net.
rollout_and_mitigation:
- Start in 'canary' availability zone with non-critical tenants; monitor dashboard.
- If health-check violation: abort shift, resume traffic to original hosts, mark dependent slices as degraded and notify SRE.
- Post-incident: capture KV warmup profile to tune warmup duration and slice size.
runbook_summary: Quick steps for on-call: 1) Identify affected slice from dashboard. 2) Execute abort-shift script to stop current traffic shaping. 3) Reassign leases to fallback hosts. 4) Scale temporary burst hosts and enable prefix caching. 5) Notify PM + customer success for impacted tenants. Full runbook link in attachments.
